baseline.name: Hash-set duplicate detection
baseline.approach: Scan values, stopping when insertion finds a value already present.
baseline.time: Expected O(n), O(n^2) worst case for an unsuitable chained table

archived.name: qsort plus adjacent equality scan
archived.time: O(n log n) if the platform qsort implementation provides that sorting bound; final scan O(n). The C standard does not prescribe qsort's worst-case complexity.
archived.space: Sorting workspace is implementation-dependent; the explicit adjacent scan uses O(1) state

why: Sorting makes duplicates adjacent and uses a standard library routine, but does not improve expected time growth over a suitable hash set.
quantitative_comparison: The archive performs one sort plus at most n-1 adjacent checks. A hash set performs at most n insert/lookups in expectation. Sorting work and workspace depend on libc; no reduction in bytes, comparisons or milliseconds is established here.
tradeoffs: The archive mutates input and its subtracting comparator relies on bounded values. Avoiding a custom hash table is a simplicity trade-off, not evidence that the solution is faster or uses less memory on this platform.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
